genZNote: The 'mild' Shigella — and the one you're actually most likely to encounter if you live somewhere with good plumbing.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human intestinal tract only — no significant animal reservoir
habitat.hostAssociation: Obligate human pathogen; low infectious dose
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Spread via fecally contaminated food, water, and person-to-person contact, notably in childcare settings

culture.colonyMorphology: Colorless colonies initially; may slowly turn pink with prolonged incubation from late lactose fermentation

identificationClues: Gram-negative, non-motile rod; the only Shigella species capable of (slow/late) lactose fermentation
ONPG positive, reflecting this delayed lactose-fermenting ability
The most common cause of shigellosis in the United States and other industrialized countries
Classic cause of outbreaks in childcare centers and among close-contact groups

diseases: Shigellosis — typically milder watery-to-bloody diarrhea compared to S. dysenteriae, though still highly contagious
virulenceFactors: Invasion of colonic epithelium via Type III secretion system
Low infectious dose enabling efficient person-to-person spread
Generally does not produce significant Shiga toxin (unlike S. dysenteriae)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Fecal-oral route; person-to-person spread is especially efficient in childcare settings, due to a very low infectious dose
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: The most frequently isolated Shigella species in the United States and other developed countries; common source of outbreaks in daycare centers, among men who have sex with men, and international travelers
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Its ability to slowly ferment lactose (unlike other Shigella species) can occasionally cause diagnostic confusion if plates aren't read at the appropriate time

examFacts.importantDisease: Shigellosis — most common Shigella species in developed countries
examFacts.importantTest: Stool culture; ONPG test reflects delayed lactose fermentation
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: The only Shigella species that ferments lactose, albeit slowly — and the most common Shigella species in industrialized countries
